tools.name: roki_search_docs
tools.description: Search the official ROKI Connect corpus (integration guide, API operations and schemas) and return ranked excerpts. Use this first when you need any ROKI-specific fact. Never answer a ROKI question from memory or from another payment gateway's conventions.

tools.name: roki_get_doc_section
tools.description: Return the complete text of one section of the integration guide, by number (e.g. "14"), sub-number ("12.1") or title fragment ("webhook").

tools.name: roki_list_operations
tools.description: List every operation the API actually exposes, plus the operations that are documented as NOT existing. Call this before writing any integration code so you never invent an endpoint.

tools.name: roki_get_operation
tools.description: Full detail for one operation: method, path, headers, request schema field table, responses, and worked examples.

tools.name: roki_get_schema
tools.description: Return a fully dereferenced JSON Schema by name (e.g. "PaymentCreateRequest", "Payment", "WebhookEvent"). Use it to know the exact field names, types and constraints.

tools.name: roki_get_error
tools.description: Explain an HTTP status or an error message returned by the ROKI API: what it means, the likely cause and what to do. Use this instead of guessing when an integration fails.

tools.name: roki_get_integration_example
tools.description: Return a complete, runnable integration example for a stack: configuration, API client, checkout flow, webhook handler with signature verification, and polling fallback.

tools.name: roki_get_quickstart
tools.description: The minimum viable integration sequence, end to end, including the manual portal steps a developer cannot skip.

tools.name: roki_get_authentication_guide
tools.description: How authentication works, how the two environments are selected, where credentials come from, and how to store and rotate them safely.

tools.name: roki_get_webhook_guide
tools.description: Everything about webhooks: portal registration, event types, payload shape, HMAC signature verification over the raw body, idempotent processing, and the polling fallback.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: roki_get_error · Private data: roki_get_authentication_guide, roki_verify_webhook_signature, roki_scaffold_integration, roki_sandbox_try, roki_status · Public sink: roki_get_doc_section, roki_check_result, roki_get_integration_example, roki_get_webhook_guide, roki_verify_webhook_signature, roki_scaffold_integration · Destructive: roki_check_result, roki_sandbox_try.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: roki_get_error · Private data: roki_get_authentication_guide, roki_verify_webhook_signature, roki_scaffold_integration, roki_sandbox_try, roki_status · Public sink: roki_get_doc_section, roki_check_result, roki_get_integration_example, roki_get_webhook_guide, roki_verify_webhook_signature, roki_scaffold_integration · Destructive: roki_check_result, roki_sandbox_try

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
